purpose: Replace a startup-only baseline with a measurement that proves continued useful firmware progress. This is not an engine performance optimization.

baseline_change.reason: The original baseline used the V1 boot ROM, which lacks the floating-point table required by the committed ELF. Replaying that ROM with the current CLI produces one frame and is accepted by the old READY/max_cycles oracle. The corrected V3 ROM produces 79 distinct frames in all three measured samples. Each timed repeat now must prove at least 75 frames and progress through 7.5 seconds of the 8-second budget.

cli_build.profile: workspace release defaults:opt3,panic abort,thin LTO,debug enabled,overflow checks enabled,event-scheduler

historical_baseline_investigation.scope: Read-only baseline provenance and normalization diagnosis; no source or baseline changes in this investigation.

baseline.comparison_to_first_parent: Only18 RTF files changed; ROM identical to first parent.

relevant_upstream_commits.change: V3 ROM, SF/SD HLE and bit operations replace the minimal V1 ROM.
Restore real workload idle fast-forward; commit explicitly identifies old accidental WFI-after-fmul.
Implement RE/RP flash erase/program; current ROM moves float tables while retaining SF/SD.
Keep USB enumeration delay-1 while IRQ high; preserve configured idle fast-forward.

static_execution_evidence: V1 __aeabi_float_init copies84bytes from missing SF lookup pointer0 into sf_table.
ELF __aeabi_fmul branches through sf_table+8, the copied NMI vector0x31.
ROM0x30 is WFI followed by branch to itself (30bffde7).

normalization.caveat: Different hosts; division cancels only a common multiplicative speed factor. Spin acceleration alone can lower this index without an absolute workload slowdown. Long-spin raw samples were not retained in these original reports.

historical_baseline_investigation.next_step: Reject old-ROM boot-only runs using existing OLED frame progress. Measure a completed workload with exact inputs and raw timing provenance before proposing a narrow baseline refresh.

same_cli_old_rom_negative_control.reason: pico_oled_pwm: OLED progress: need >= 75 unique meaningful frames and last >= 7500000 us; observed 1, last=101531

rejudgment.method: Rejudge the retained measured samples against their replacement reference; this is not another runtime execution.

limits: The wall-clock measurement was made on a shared local host, not the GitHub Ubuntu24.04 runner. CI acceptance of the final tree remains pending.
The normalized index cancels only common host scaling; raw workload and spin samples are retained.
No firmware, RP2040 descriptor, ROM, or engine implementation was changed for this benchmark repair.
The existing 1x CPU-spin RTx floor and 25% normalized workload RTF tolerance remain unchanged.

fresh_verification_after_rebaseline.interpretation: This is a separate real execution against the fixed reference. All three workload samples prove 79 frames, and both existing performance thresholds pass.

measurement_notes: The long spin targets about one wall second using short-run RTx. The recorded reference samples actually took 0.338 to 0.434 seconds; use their raw values, not the target, when reproducing the index.
Final source edits after the fresh verification only correct comments/docstrings and add this receipt; measurement code behavior is unchanged.
